# Cold read of commit 23f18f024, coordinator skill (draft 12)

Read as the coordinating session. Parts read whole: `SKILL.md` and `references/skill-rewrite.md`. The changed text: `SKILL.md` lines 125 and 126; `skill-rewrite.md` lines 19 to 21 (step 7) and line 24. The change to `references/sources.md` is not a rule (`SKILL.md` line 124), so it is not judged.

## 1. The lint's output

`python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py .claude/skills/coordinator/SKILL.md .claude/skills/coordinator/references/skill-rewrite.md` printed nothing, exit 0. No lint hits.

## 2. What the session would do differently, section by section

- `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", line 125: after a change to this skill lands, I would brief a worker to update the page of skill drafts, then send the curator one line with the page's link, instead of the old words, the new words and the reason in chat. I would take a reversal from a comment on the page's item as well as from chat.
- Line 126: I would put a waiting change under the page's section "Proposed changes". I would no longer read an order to remove landed items.
- `skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7: I would brief the worker to keep two sections on the page: the last landing's changes as diffs with their reasons, and the waiting items.
- Line 24: no change of action; it points to step 7.

Repair history or detail that changes no action: none found in the changed text.

## 3. Flags

### `references/skill-rewrite.md`

**F1. Line 19 and line 20, "after each landing" and "the last landing".** Kind: a sentence that reads two ways; one word for one thing. Confidence: high.
In this skill "landing" names a batch's landing: line 29 of the same part, "After each landing, the orientation workflow updates ...", and `SKILL.md` line 247, "At a landing". Step 7 uses the same word for a skill change landing. A session reading "after each landing" can update the page after every batch landing, or wait for one, and cannot tell what "the last landing" covers when a writer's task makes several commits, or the cold read's fixes land as a second commit.
Fix, restate: "7. For the coordinator skill, after each change lands, have a worker update the page of skill drafts." and "Landed changes: one item for each change that landed since the curator last saw the page." (Or define one skill landing, such as "the commits of one writer task, pushed together".)

**F2. Line 20, "one item for each change of the last landing", against `SKILL.md` line 179 ("Quiet times").** Kind: a gotcha. Confidence: high.
"Quiet times" holds the reports of skill changes while the curator is away and sends them in one message on return. If two skill changes land while the curator is away, the second update replaces the first landing's items, so the curator, when back, sees only the last landing's diffs and the held one-line reports point to a page that no longer shows the earlier change. Nothing reads the earlier change, which is the failure that line 125's last sentence names.
Fix, restate: "Landed changes: one item for each change that landed since the curator last read the page. Clear the section only after the curator has read it." Or keep each landing as its own subsection, newest first.

**F3. Line 20, "with the old words struck through", against `SKILL.md` lines 196 to 199 ("Pages").** Kind: clash with a rule elsewhere. Confidence: medium.
"Pages" says an item holds its new text whole with the added words marked, then its current text collapsed, then what the change alters and why. Step 7 asks for the new words with the old words struck through, and says nothing of marking the added words or of the collapsed current text. After a landing, "its current text" is the new text, so the "Pages" order no longer fits. A worker briefed from both does one of three things: strike-through only, marking only, or both with a collapsed copy of the same text. The session cannot tell which rule wins.
Fix, restate in step 7: "The item follows "Pages" in `SKILL.md`, with one difference: in place of the collapsed current text, it shows the old words struck through within the new text." Or add to "Pages" one line that a landed item marks the added words and strikes the old ones, and has no collapsed text.

**F4. Line 20, "against the text that the curator approved on the page, or else the text before the change".** Kind: a sentence that reads two ways. Confidence: medium.
It does not say when the first case applies. It can read as: for a change that waited for the curator's yes, the diff is against the approved draft (so it shows only what the writer changed after the yes); or: against whatever version of the section the curator last approved on the page, for every change. A worker may then diff a change against an old approved draft and show words that never stood in the skill.
Fix, restate: "For a change that waited for the curator's yes, diff it against the words that the curator approved, so that the item shows only what changed after the yes. For any other change, diff it against the skill's text before the change."

**F5. Line 20, "such as a cold read's flag or the lint".** Kind: a term not defined where it is used. Confidence: low.
"The lint" appears nowhere else in the coordinator skill. The session that knows the cold-read brief knows it; a fresh session after a compaction does not.
Fix: "such as a cold read's flag or a hit of the skills lint (`explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py`)", or drop "or the lint".

**F6. Line 19, "have a worker update the page of skill drafts".** Kind: a gotcha. Confidence: medium.
The step does not say what the worker's brief holds. `SKILL.md` line 204 says that a publish by source path alone makes a new page, and line 202 sets the house style. A worker briefed with "update the page" and no URL, no commit range and no house style makes a new page, and the boot note's link then points to a stale page.
Fix, add a sentence: "Brief it with the page's URL from the boot note, the commits of the change, and the house style of "Pages"; it publishes by that URL."

**F7. Line 24, "You push, and keep the page of the change in step ... the page of skill drafts for the coordinator skill (step 7)."** Kind: none of the list beyond a small doubt; one subject for one act. Confidence: low.
Line 24 says "you" keep the page in step; step 7 and `SKILL.md` line 125 say a worker updates it. Read together, "keep in step" means "have a worker update", which is plain enough. The pointer to step 7 holds. Optional fix: "... the page of skill drafts for the coordinator skill, by a worker (step 7)."

### `SKILL.md`

**F8. Line 125, "by a comment on its item or in chat, have the skill writer restore the old words at once", against line 191 ("While the curator reads turn by turn").** Kind: clash with a rule elsewhere. Confidence: medium.
Line 191 says that while the curator comments on a page, each comment's turn is "." in chat and the point is kept until the reading is done, except "a comment that needs work now". Line 125 says a reversal is acted on at once. A session can hold a reversal comment until the reading ends. The exception in line 191 probably covers it, but the session must infer that.
Fix, restate the end of line 125's sentence: "... have the skill writer restore the old words at once, with no cold read, also while the curator is still commenting on the page."

**F9. Line 125, "by a comment on its item".** Kind: a gotcha. Confidence: medium.
If a worker publishes the page, nothing in the change says how a comment on the item reaches this session. A session that does not watch the page for comments misses the reversal, and the change stays.
Fix, add: "Watch the page for the curator's comments after each update."

**F10. Line 125, "Then tell the curator in one line, in your next message, with the page's link."** Kind: a sentence that reads two ways. Confidence: low.
It does not say what the line names. A session can send "skill page updated" alone, and the curator cannot tell from the line whether the change touches what he cares about. Also, "Then" makes the message wait for the worker; if the session's next message comes first, it is unclear whether to wait or send the line later.
Fix, restate: "When the worker is done, tell the curator in one line, in your next message: the file and section that changed, and the page's link."

**F11. Line 126, "Put it as an item under the page's proposed changes."** Kind: a sentence that reads two ways (weak). Confidence: low.
"The page" leans on the bullet before it. The old text said "the page of skill drafts, whose link the boot note holds", and also "remove the items that have landed"; that order is gone, and step 7 only implies it ("the items that wait"). A session can leave an approved item under "Proposed changes" after it lands, beside its diff under "Landed changes".
Fix, restate: "Put it as an item under "Proposed changes" on the page of skill drafts. When it lands, its item moves to "Landed changes"."

**F12. Line 125 and line 179 ("Quiet times"), "Hold the reports of skill changes until the curator is back, and send them then in one message."** Kind: clash (small). Confidence: low.
The report is now one line with a link, and a worker's update of the page is not a message to the curator, so the two rules fit: the page update goes on, the line waits. But "send them then in one message" now means several one-liners with the same link. With F2 fixed this is harmless; without it, the held lines point to a page that lost the earlier items. No separate fix beyond F2; optionally in line 179: "... and send them then in one line with the page's link."

## 4. Pointers

- `SKILL.md` line 125, "(`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7)": holds; step 7 is at `skill-rewrite.md` line 19.
- `SKILL.md` line 125, "whose link the boot note holds": holds by line 216, which puts the URLs of live pages in the boot note. The boot note's own content was not read, as the brief says.

- `SKILL.md` line 124, "unless the bullet after next says that it waits": still holds; the bullet after next is line 126.
- `skill-rewrite.md` line 24, "(step 7)": holds.

## 5. Register

Plain full sentences hold throughout. One word for one thing breaks at "landing" (F1). No shorthand. "The lint" is undefined (F5). No source or decision status is named in the changed text of `SKILL.md` or `skill-rewrite.md`.

## 6. Undefined terms

- "the lint": `skill-rewrite.md` line 20.
- "landing" in the sense of a skill change: `skill-rewrite.md` line 19 (elsewhere the word means a batch's landing).
- "page of skill drafts": not in the glossary; first used before this change (`skill-rewrite.md` line 16), and line 125 now locates it by the boot note. Not a flag of this change.

## 7. Gotchas

- Two skill landings while the curator is away: the page shows only the last (F2).
- A worker briefed without the page's URL makes a new page (F6).
- A reversal comment on the page is not seen, or is held until the reading ends (F8, F9).

## 13. A page of its own for the changes to `fortress-repo` (held 11-05 12:0x)

Line numbers are those of `main` at `f1dff89b4`.

**Proposed text.** In `coordinator/SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", the fourth bullet (line 127) becomes:

> - Change the other skills by the method of `references/skill-rewrite.md`. A new rule, or a change of a rule's meaning, waits for the curator's word, as its step 6 says. For `fortress-repo`, put such a change as an item under "Proposed changes" on the page of `fortress-repo` changes, whose link the boot note holds. After any other change to `fortress-repo` lands, by your skill writer or by the record-landing workflow, a worker updates that page (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7). Report it and take a reversal as the second bullet says for this skill. For `cloud-container`, tell the curator when a change lands: what changed, why, what it fixes, and any risk to watch for.

In `coordinator/references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 4 becomes:

> 4. For `cloud-container`, publish the part as a page; the curator reads it whole. For the coordinator skill and `fortress-repo`, land the change after its cold read, or put it on the skill's page, as `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", says.

Step 6, its second sentence becomes:

> On the other skills, a change waits for the curator only where a rule would change its meaning or a new rule would enter; for `fortress-repo`, put it on the skill's page.

Step 7 becomes:

> 7. After each change to the coordinator skill or to `fortress-repo` lands, have a worker update that skill's page: the page of skill drafts for the coordinator skill, the page of `fortress-repo` changes for `fortress-repo`. The boot note holds both links. Give the worker the page's URL, and have it publish by that URL. The record-landing workflow runs this update itself for the changes to `fortress-repo` that follow a landing (`references/batch.md`, "The landing", step 4). Each page has two sections:
>    - Landed changes: one item for each change that landed since the curator's last approval on the page, or since the curator last said that they had read it, so that no change lands unseen while the curator is away. The item takes the form of a landed item in `SKILL.md`, "Pages". For a change that waited for the curator's yes, it shows the change against the words that the curator approved. For any other change, it shows the change against the skill's text before it. It gives the change's reason, such as a cold read's flag, a hit of the skills' lint, `explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py`, or the record entry that the orientation update took in.
>    - Proposed changes: the items that wait for the curator's yes. An approved item leaves this section when it lands, and appears under the landed changes.

The bullet after the steps (line 24), its second sentence becomes:

> You push, and keep the page of the change in step: the part's page for `cloud-container`, and for the coordinator skill and `fortress-repo` the skill's page, by a worker (step 7).

In `coordinator/references/batch.md`, "The landing", step 4, its first paragraph (line 94) becomes:

> 4. After the post-batch review is committed, run the record-landing workflow (`explorations/coordinator/tools/record-landing/README.md`). It brings FACTS, POSITIONS, INDEX, PLAN and the review queue in line with the landing. It lands its commits on `main` and pushes them. Then it runs the orientation workflow in update mode itself, on the entries that the landing added or changed. The orientation workflow writes new text for each section of `fortress-repo`'s `revival-changes.md` that these entries touch. Next, the workflow has the skill writer install the sections that the orientation judge accepts, and bring `fortress-repo`'s other parts in line with the landing. It runs a cold read of these changes, and the writer fixes its flags. Last, it has a worker update the page of `fortress-repo` changes (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7). No step of yours comes between.

The second paragraph of step 4, its third sentence, gains a sentence after it:

> Send the curator the one line for the page of `fortress-repo` changes, as `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", says.

**Current text.**
- `SKILL.md`, line 127: "Change the other skills by the method of `references/skill-rewrite.md`. A new rule, or a change of a rule's meaning, waits for the curator's word, as its step 6 says. Tell the curator when any other change lands: what changed, why, what it fixes, and any risk to watch for."
- `skill-rewrite.md`, step 4: "4. For the other skills, publish the part as a page; the curator reads it whole. For the coordinator skill, land the change after its cold read, or put it on the page of skill drafts, as `SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions", says."
- Step 6, second sentence: "On the other skills, ask the curator only where a rule would change its meaning or a new rule would enter."
- Step 7: "7. For the coordinator skill, after each change lands, have a worker update the page of skill drafts. Give it the page's URL from the boot note, and have it publish by that URL. The page has two sections:" with the two sections as now (the reason's examples: "such as a cold read's flag or a hit of the skills' lint, `explorations/coordinator/tools/skills-lint.py`").
- The bullet after the steps, second sentence: "You push, and keep the page of the change in step: the part's page for the other skills, the page of skill drafts for the coordinator skill, by a worker (step 7)."
- `batch.md`, step 4, first paragraph: "… Then it runs the orientation workflow in update mode itself, on the entries that the landing added or changed. No step of yours comes between. The orientation workflow writes new text for each section of `fortress-repo`'s `revival-changes.md` that these entries touch. Have the writer install the sections that its judge accepts (`references/skill-rewrite.md`)."

**What it changes, and why.** `fortress-repo` gets a page of the same form as the page of skill drafts. A worker updates it after every change to that skill lands, and the record-landing workflow runs that update itself at its end. The chat gets one line with the commit and the link. The curator sees what the landings change in the worker skill, which every worker reads, as he now sees the coordinator skill's changes. A new rule or a changed meaning still waits for his word, now as an item on that page. Steps 4 and 6 and the bullet after the steps change with step 7, so that no line of the method still sends a `fortress-repo` change to a page of the whole part, or to an ask in chat.

**Ground.**
- Held 11-05 12:0x: "the same page treatment for the `fortress-repo` skill, so that when the post-landing process updates it (the orientation workflow's update of the revival part, the skill writer's changes to the area parts, their cold read), a page shows him the landed diffs with reasons; and make it part of the landing workflow, after the skill writer has updated the skills from the landed changes."
- The coordinator's task of 11-05: one page for each skill, the links in the boot note; the chat's one line with the commit and the link; what waits stays as `SKILL.md`'s fourth bullet says.

**Where the record does not settle it.**
- The workflow today ends with the orientation update: the skill writer's install, its pass over the area parts and their cold read are steps of the coordinator's, and no worker updates a page. The new `batch.md` text states the chain as it will stand once it is built into the workflow. I lean to landing that paragraph only with the workflow's change, as the coordinator's plan orders it. The other reading lands it now, so the coordinator runs the missing steps by hand until the workflow does.
- `cloud-container`: I lean to keeping its old report, since the ask names `fortress-repo` only. The other reading gives every skill a page.
- Who pushes the skill writer's commits inside the workflow: today the writer commits and the coordinator pushes (bullet after the steps). Once the workflow runs the writer, the workflow would push them, as it pushes the record's commits. The draft does not say so; the workflow's README is the place.
- Steps 4 and 6 and the bullet after the steps are not named in the task. I changed them because their words would otherwise still send a `fortress-repo` change to a page of the whole part, or to an ask in chat.

The sentence before it sends the POSITIONS report "as `SKILL.md`, "Quiet times", says", and "Quiet times" (line 179) holds the reports of skill changes while the curator is away. `SKILL.md` line 127 says "in your next message". Kind: a gotcha; a clash. A landing often ends in a turn that a check-in started, when the curator is away. What the reader does wrong: it sends the one line at once in that turn, against "Quiet times", because the nearer text says "next message" and names only "The curator's role a
31:**Flag 5. "The commit" when the workflow made several.** `SKILL.md` line 127, "with the commit and the page's link", which line 96 points to. Inside the workflow a `fortress-repo` change is several commits: the installed sections, the other parts, the writer's fixes. Kind: a sentence that reads two ways. What the reader does wrong: it names one commit, for example the last fix, and the curator reads a part of the change on GitHub. Confidence: medium. Fix: in line 127, "with the commit, or for the workflow's changes the first and last commit, and the page's link".
35:**Flag 6. Line 127 repeats line 125 nearly word for word.** Line 127: "Tell the curator in one line, in your next message, with the commit and the page's link. The two copies already differ: line 125 has "When the worker is done", "Watch the page for comments sent to Claude" and "The reversal does not wait for the end of the curator's reading"; line 127 has none of them. The curator approved the page with the caveat that it is only a surface for checking, and changes nothing in how `fortress-repo` is updated. The skill does not say so. The page of skill drafts, right above in line 125 and 126, is the page where changes wait for his yes. Kind: a gotcha. What the reader does wrong: by analogy it waits for the curator's read of the `fortress-repo` page before the next change, or puts a proposed `fortress-repo` change on it, or takes his silence on the page as his word on a change of meaning. Confidence: medium. Fix: restate "The page lets the curat
39:**Flag 8. "Your skill writer".** Line 127: "by your skill writer or by the record-landing workflow". Line 124 and `batch.md` line 94 say "the skill writer"; `skill-rewrite.md` says "the writer". Kind: register, one word for one thing. What the reader does wrong: it reads two writers, the one it runs and one inside the workflow, and wonders whether the second follows the same brief. If two are meant, the skill does not say how they differ. Confidence: low. Fix: "by the skill writer, whether you run it or the record-landing workflow does".
41:**Flag 9. "A worker updates" where the rest says "have a worker update".** Line 127: "a worker updates the page of `fortress-repo` changes". Line 125 and `skill-rewrite.md` step 7 tell the coordinator to "have a worker update". Kind: a sentence that reads two ways. What the reader does wrong: when the coordinator's own writer made the change, it reads the passive as something that happens without it and launches no worker. Confidence: low; the pointer to step 7 settles it for a reader who follows it. Fix: covered by flag 6; otherwise "have a worker update the page ..., unless the record-landing workflow made the change, which runs the update itself".
43:**Flag 10. The plain-words rule has two homes, and "a ruling's number" is unclear.** Line 200: "The reason says in plain words what was wrong and what the text now says. "Both by a worker" after three pages.** Line 24: "the part's page for the other skills, the page of skill drafts for the coordinator skill, and the page of `fortress-repo` changes for `fortress-repo`, both by a worker (step 7)." Kind: a sentence that reads two ways. Three pages are listed, so "both" points at two of them by guess. "The other skills" also includes `fortress-repo`, so the line can be read as `fortress-repo` having a part's page and the changes page, or only the changes page. Step 4 still says "For the other skills, publish the part as a page; the curator reads it whole", and the caveat says the new page changes nothing in that. What the reader does wrong: it drop
49:**Flag 12. Fix: add "On the page of `fortress-repo` changes, which holds no approvals, it is each change since the curator last said that he had read the page."

Elsewhere the skill says "the orientation workflow in update mode" (`batch.md` line 94, `record.md` line 110). Kind: register, one word for one thing. What the reader does wrong: little; it may wonder whether this is a separate step. Confidence: low. Fix: "or the record entry that the orientation workflow, in update mode, took in".
